breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a clear sky to close the week strong. Fierce calm is Friday composure under cloud: charge first, body second, two clean must-dos, quiet admin only after the morning has already won. Competitive. Unbeatable. bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: The cloud is a cloak, not a cage
items.body: Friday overcast is classic veil weather in the old books — gray that hides the sun and sharpens the inner lamp. Gnostic operators treat the cloak as cover for clean action, not an excuse to wait. What you cannot see outside is exactly when you practice seeing what you already carry.

Hermetic calendars mark the week’s close as a seal, not a collapse. Seal the day with breath and one finished must-do before you open the noise. A sealed Friday becomes Monday’s head start; an unsealed Friday leaks into the weekend.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.hed: Close the ring before you open the gate
grimoire.body: Solomon’s circles were not superstition — they were boundaries. A king who invites counsel before the court is set loses the throne to the first loud voice. Your Friday morning is that court: breath draws the ring, body stands inside it, then the desks may enter. Close first. Then open.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, name one must-do out loud. Then start the 3-minute opener. Do not open mail until both are done.

image.alt: Newsprint diagram — Delegate not Operate: persistent computer, memory, tools

lesson.oneLiner: If the bot already has a computer, stop piloting every click — design the handoff, then leave.
beats: Computer — Grok Bot runs on a persistent cloud machine (browser, filesystem, tools), not your laptop session.
Memory — work survives when you close the lid; agents keep going overnight.
Delegate — your job is the brief and the gate, not operating every step.
Boundary — separate bots on the same account share one computer; do not treat them as isolated security boxes.
Rule: one clear outcome + one review window beats twenty ‘just checking’ interruptions.
lesson.takeaway: Operator leverage compounds when you stop being the bottleneck. @mmmik000: brief → delegate → review. Then get back to the board.
